trials.name: Clarity AD
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline in the CDR-SB at 18 Months
trials.results_summary: Results published in NEJM (2023) showed a statistically significant but numerically modest slowing of clinical decline on the CDR-SB scale at 18 months, with a notable incidence of ARIA.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) (Overall Population)
trials.results_summary: Results published in JAMA (2023) demonstrated a slowing of clinical and functional decline at 18 months, alongside substantial rates of ARIA.

trials.name: EMERGE
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score at Week 78
trials.results_summary: Trial was halted early for futility; later post-hoc analyses suggested marginal benefit in a high-dose subgroup, leading to controversial accelerated approval which was later discontinued.

trials.name: ENGAGE
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score at Week 78
trials.results_summary: Trial halted early for futility; failed to demonstrate a significant clinical benefit on the primary efficacy endpoint.

trials.name: GRADUATE I
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Global Outcome, as Measured by CDR-SB
trials.results_summary: Trial failed to meet its primary endpoint of significantly slowing clinical decline, resulting in the termination of the drug's development program.

trials.name: GRADUATE II
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline to Week 116 in Global Outcome, as Measured by CDR-SB
trials.results_summary: Failed to meet the primary efficacy endpoint, leading to discontinuation of the clinical program.

trials.name: EXPEDITION 3
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive 14 Item Subscore (ADAS-Cog14)
trials.results_summary: Trial failed to meet its primary endpoint; the drug did not significantly slow cognitive decline compared to placebo.

related_evidence.description: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (Clarity AD results published in NEJM)
Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial (published in JAMA)
The Problem of Aducanumab for the Treatment of Alzheimer Disease (Editorial in Ann Intern Med analyzing the controversial FDA approval)

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence record robustly supports the review's central claims regarding trivial absolute clinical benefits and concerning safety risks. While recent pivotal phase 3 trials for lecanemab (Clarity AD) and donanemab (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2) met their primary endpoints with statistical significance, the absolute differences on clinical scales were numerically small (e.g. fractional point differences on the 18-point CDR-SB scale) and fall below widely accepted thresholds for clinical meaningfulness. Furthermore, earlier programs involving aducanumab, gantenerumab, and solanezumab were terminated after failing to demonstrate efficacy. The registry records confirm a consistently high incidence of ARIA across the class, substantiating the authors' conclusion of an unfavorable risk-benefit profile for anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies in early Alzheimer's disease.
discrepancies: No factual discrepancies were found between the registry records and the Cochrane review's meta-analysis.
The review accurately reports and pools the clinical endpoint values that were published in primary readouts, accurately reflecting the small absolute effect sizes observed in these trials.
